title: Tool wear in a milling trial (forward selection)
intro:
A milling trial cut 20 test blocks and measured the flank wear of the tool (µm) after each. Four settings varied: cutting speed (m/min), feed (mm per tooth), depth of cut (mm) and coolant flow (L/min). Use **forward selection**: start with no predictors and add, one at a time, the predictor with the smallest p-value while that p-value is below 0.05.

Find how many predictors forward selection keeps (the regression degrees of freedom, k), the adjusted R² of the model it chooses, and that model's residual standard error σ̂. Give adjusted R² to four decimals and σ̂ to two decimals; k is a whole number.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **Multiple regression**, set **Data table** to the table you pasted, **Response column (y)** to *Wear*, **Predictor columns** to *Speed, Feed, Depth, Coolant* and **Variable selection** to *Forward selection (add while p < 0.05)*. Read **Selection** to see each step. Ctrl+L brings you back.

DfRegression.says: That is all four candidates. Forward selection adds a predictor only while its p-value is below 0.05; read the Selection line to see where it stopped.
Check the third step: the best remaining predictor's p-value there is not below 0.05, so forward selection stops before adding it.

AdjustedRSquared.says: That is the adjusted R² of the model with all four predictors. Forward selection kept fewer; give the adjusted R² of its model.
That is R² of the chosen model. The question asks adjusted R².

ResidualSe.says: That is σ̂ of the model with all four predictors. Give σ̂ of the model forward selection chose.

hints: Step 1 fits four one-predictor models and adds the predictor with the smallest p-value, if it is below 0.05.
Each later step tries every remaining predictor alongside those already in, and adds the best one only if its p-value is below 0.05.
When it stops, the regression degrees of freedom equal the number of predictors in the model; adjusted R² and σ̂ are those of that model.
